legend.title: What the statuses mean
legend.intro: The same colours mean the same thing everywhere: green is fine, amber needs attention, red is broken, grey is unknown.
legend.history: History: how did a sync end?
legend.actions: Plan actions: what a sync will do

Synced.label: Synced
Synced.description: Discord matches the active revision in git.

OutOfSync.label: Out of sync
OutOfSync.description: Discord differs from the active revision. The next sync applies the plan.

Unknown.label: Unknown
Unknown.description: Not compared yet: no bot connected or no sync so far.

Progressing.label: Progressing
Progressing.description: Starting or syncing; it should settle shortly.

Degraded.label: Degraded
Degraded.description: The last operation failed. The message explains why and how to fix it.

Missing.label: Missing
Missing.description: Not running: the bot is not connected or the server is not reachable.

failed.label: Failed
failed.description: Discord refused one or more changes. Nothing else was rolled back.

rejected.label: Rejected
rejected.description: The revision is invalid; the runtime kept the last valid one.

paused.label: Paused
paused.description: Enforcement was paused on the server: nothing is applied to it until it is resumed.

resumed.label: Resumed
resumed.description: Enforcement was resumed: the next revision or sync applies the configuration again.

skipped.label: Not applied
skipped.description: The revision was activated, but not applied to this server because enforcement is paused.

create.label: Create
create.description: Declared in YAML, missing on Discord: it will be created.

update.label: Update
update.description: Exists on Discord with different values: they will be changed.

delete.label: Delete
delete.description: Removed from YAML and pruning is on: it will be deleted on Discord.

adopt.label: Adopt
adopt.description: An existing resource with the same name becomes managed by Cicord.

reorder.label: Reorder
reorder.description: Positions will be changed to follow the YAML order.

unmanage.label: Unmanage
unmanage.description: Removed from YAML: Cicord stops managing it but leaves it on Discord.

blocked.label: Blocked
blocked.description: A safety rule prevents this change; it is not applied.

errors.otherFailures_one: {{count}} other change failed in the same sync.
errors.otherFailures_other: {{count}} other changes failed in the same sync.

network.title: Can't reach the runtime
network.message: The Cicord runtime did not answer.
network.hint: Check that cicord is running and reachable, then retry.

forbidden.title: Not available with your role
forbidden.message: Your role on this server does not allow this.
forbidden.hint: Ask a server admin for access (spec.access in the server YAML).

notFound.title: Not found
notFound.message: It may have been removed from the repository.

conflict.title: Changed since you opened it
conflict.message: Someone changed the configuration in the meantime.
conflict.hint: Reload to get the latest version, then redo your change.

invalid.title: Some values are invalid
invalid.hint: Fix the highlighted fields and try again.

unavailable.message: The runtime cannot do this right now.
unavailable.hint: Check the bot status, then retry in a moment.

internal.title: The runtime hit an internal error
internal.message: This is a bug in Cicord, not in your configuration.
internal.hint: Retry; if it persists, check the runtime logs.

blocked.title: Blocked
blocked.text: Safety rules prevent these operations. They are not applied.

blockedReason.deletionProtection: Removed from the YAML, but deletion protection is on (syncPolicy.deletionProtection).

boost.title: Waiting for boosts
boost.text: These changes need a higher server boost level; the server stays in sync meanwhile. Once the level is reached, Cicord applies them right away with selfHeal; otherwise they show as pending until the next revision or Sync now.

policy.title: Sync policy
policy.description: How Cicord reconciles Discord with git.
policy.selfHealHelp: On: changes made on Discord are reverted as soon as they are seen (gateway events and the periodic resync). Off: they are shown as drift until the next revision or Sync now. Nothing is reverted while enforcement is paused.
policy.pruneHelp: Delete resources removed from the YAML (otherwise they are only unmanaged).
policy.deletionProtectionHelp: Block every deletion, even with prune on.

setup.title: Set up Cicord
setup.simulatorHint: This runtime uses the Discord simulator: the buttons marked “Simulate” stand in for what you would do on discord.com.

access.title: Open the setup link
access.text: For security, the setup wizard only opens with the one-time link Cicord printed in its logs when it started. It looks like {{example}}.
access.placeholder: Paste the link from the logs

welcome.title: Let's get your Discord server running on Cicord
welcome.lead: In about ten minutes, Cicord will manage your server's roles, channels and permissions, and run plugins like welcome messages or tickets. Every change is saved as a version you can review or undo.

items.bot: You create a Discord bot and paste its token: Cicord checks it and finds everything else itself.
items.invite: You add the bot to your server with one link. Cicord checks it has the rights it needs.
items.import: Cicord reads your server as it is today and saves it. Nothing on Discord changes.
items.verify: Cicord verifies everything live, then you can add a first plugin.

welcome.question: Where are you starting from?
welcome.existing: I already have a Discord server
welcome.existingText: Cicord adopts your roles and channels as they are.
welcome.newText: Create an empty server first, Cicord takes it from there.
welcome.newSteps: In Discord, click the “+” at the bottom of your server list → “Create My Own” → give it a name. Come back here once it exists.

discord.title: Create your bot
discord.lead: A bot is how Cicord acts on your server. You create it once in Discord's Developer Portal; it takes two minutes.
discord.step1: Open the Developer Portal and click “New Application”. The name you choose is your bot's name (you can change it later). Accept the terms and click “Create”.
discord.step2: In the left menu, open “Bot”, click “Reset Token”, confirm, then click “Copy”. Discord shows the token only once.
discord.step3: Paste the token below. Cicord checks it with Discord and stores it encrypted; it is never shown again.
discord.tokenPlaceholder: Paste the token copied from the Bot page
discord.tokenHelp: It is a long text with two dots. Not the Application ID, not the Client Secret.
discord.simCreated: A simulated bot was created and its token pasted below.
discord.intentsLead: Some plugins need to see who joins the server or what messages say. Discord asks you to turn these on explicitly.
discord.intentToggles: On the Bot page, scroll to “Privileged Gateway Intents” and turn on:

server.title: Add the bot to your server
server.lead: Open the invite link, choose your server and click “Authorize”. Keep “Administrator” checked: Cicord manages roles, channels and permissions for you.
server.inviteDetails: Asks for the “bot” and “applications.commands” scopes with the Administrator permission.
server.simLow: Place the bot's role at the bottom (to try the fix)
server.watching: Watching for new servers… it appears here a few seconds after you click Authorize.
server.none: The bot is not in any server yet.
server.noManage: You need the “Manage Server” permission on a server to add a bot to it. Usually the server owner does it.
server.simRaise: Simulate: drag the bot role to the top
server.accessAdminText: Cicord can manage everything right away. Anyone holding the bot token controls the whole server.
server.accessInspectText: The bot joins with View Channels only. Review what Cicord sees and the first plan, with no change on Discord, then grant more or stop.
server.inviteDetailsInspect: Asks for the “bot” and “applications.commands” scopes with the View Channels permission only.

inspect.title: Inspection of {{name}}
inspect.lead: Read-only: Cicord imported the server into a temporary copy and planned it. Nothing is saved yet.
inspect.nothingChanged: Nothing was changed on Discord: {{reads}} read calls, {{writes}} write calls.
inspect.admin: The bot is Administrator: it sees and can change everything.
inspect.hiddenNone: None: as Administrator, the bot can view every category and channel.
inspect.hiddenLead: Listed by Discord, but the bot cannot open them or read their messages:
inspect.unlisted_one: {{count}} channel the server refers to is not listed ({{refs}}).
inspect.unlisted_other: {{count}} channels the server refers to are not listed ({{refs}}).
inspect.omitted: Discord leaves the channels a bot cannot view out of the channel list: private channels the bot is not allowed in may be missing here and are not imported. To manage one, allow View Channel and Manage Channels to the bot's role in it, then inspect again.
inspect.unreadableNone: Nothing: every part of the server was read.
inspect.unreadableLead: Left out of the configuration, so Cicord would not manage them. Grant the permission and inspect again to include them.
inspect.needsTitle: To apply changes, the bot would also need
inspect.needsNone: Nothing: the bot already has every permission this configuration needs.
inspect.planEmpty: No changes: Cicord would adopt everything as it is.
inspect.planIncomplete_one: {{count}} change, because the bot cannot see a channel the server refers to. Do not apply it: let the bot view that channel and inspect again.
inspect.planIncomplete_other: {{count}} changes, because the bot cannot see channels the server refers to. Do not apply them: let the bot view those channels and inspect again.
inspect.stopText: Nothing was changed on Discord and no configuration was saved. To remove the bot, kick it from the server in Discord.
inspect.upgradeTitle: Continue: give the bot more access
inspect.upgradeText: Authorize one of these links for the same server (it updates the bot's role), then re-check.

repo.title: Where should Cicord keep your configuration?
repo.lead: Cicord saves your server's setup as files. Every change made in the admin is a new version, so you can see what changed and go back.

providers.embeddedText: Stored by Cicord next to its data, with full history. No git or GitHub account needed.
providers.githubText: For teams who review changes on GitHub. Cicord pushes the first version for you.
providers.localText: Development: the files are written to the folder “cicord dev” watches; edit them in your editor.

repo.urlHelp: Create an empty repository on GitHub first (it can be private).
repo.tokenHelp: Create a fine-grained token on this repository with “Contents: Read and write”, plus “Pull requests” and “Commit statuses: Read and write” for reviews and sync statuses. It is stored encrypted.
repo.appHelp: A GitHub App acts as its own bot account with short-lived tokens. Give it “Contents”, “Pull requests” and “Commit statuses: Read and write” (and “Metadata: Read”), then install it on this repository.
repo.installationIdHelp: Cicord finds it from the repository. Enter it only if that fails: it is the number at the end of the installation's settings URL.
repo.privateKeyPlaceholder: Paste the .pem file generated on the App's page (Private keys → Generate a private key)
repo.privateKeyStored: A private key is stored; paste another one to replace it
repo.privateKeyHelp: Cicord checks it by getting a token for the repository. It is stored encrypted.
repo.importLead: Cicord reads {{name}} as it is today (roles, channels, permissions) and saves it as the first version. Nothing changes on Discord.
repo.activated: Your server is now managed by Cicord
repo.proof: Proof: Cicord compared the saved configuration with Discord and found nothing to change.
repo.proofChanges_one: Cicord found {{count}} difference between the configuration and Discord.
repo.proofChanges_other: Cicord found {{count}} differences between the configuration and Discord.
repo.needsConfirm: Applying this configuration would change Discord
repo.needsConfirmText: Usually the import adopts everything as it is. Review these changes before applying them.

login.title: Sign in to the admin with Discord
login.lead: Optional but recommended: lets you (and your moderators) sign in to this admin console with Discord. Server owners are admins automatically.
login.step1: Open the OAuth2 page of your application.
login.step2: Under “Redirects”, click “Add Redirect”, paste this URL, then “Save Changes”:
login.step3: Click “Reset Secret”, copy the Client Secret and paste it below.
login.fromEnv: The client secret comes from the CICORD_DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET environment variable.
login.testing: Waiting for the login in the other tab…
login.returnText: You can close this tab and go back to the setup wizard.
login.simText: With the simulator, you sign in with “dev login” (any simulated user): nothing to configure here.
login.skipWarning: Without it, only the setup link can open the admin. You can configure it later (CICORD_DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET).

verify.title: Let's check everything works
verify.lead: Cicord runs these checks live. Fix anything red, then they update on their own.
verify.sendMessage: Send a message in any channel of {{name}} (for example “hello Cicord”). This proves Cicord receives events from Discord.

plugin.title: Add your first plugin
plugin.lead: Plugins are the features of your bot. Pick one to try; you can add more later from the admin.
plugin.tryIt: Try it now: type /{{command}} in a channel of {{server}}.
plugin.noCommand: It reacts to what happens on your server.
plugin.pr: A pull request was opened: the plugin is active once it is merged.

done.title: You're all set
done.adminText: Roles, channels, plugins, history and diagnostics.
done.loginWarning: Admin login is not configured: once you finish, the setup link stops working. Configure Discord login first, or set CICORD_DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET later.

sources.name: Name

confirmRemove.text: Its plugins can no longer be installed. This changes cicord.yaml for the whole project. Instances already using the source block the removal.

forbidden.title: You cannot change the sources
forbidden.text: Sources live in cicord.yaml and apply to the whole project: adding or removing one needs the admin role on every server Cicord manages.

result.prText: The change applies once the pull request is merged.

sources.privateTip: This registry needs an access token, kept in the runtime's secret store.
sources.signedTip: The index of this official registry is signed by an official Cicord key.
sources.badSignatureTip: The index of this official registry has no valid signature by an official Cicord key: its plugins are not listed.

token.dialogText: Cicord checks that the registry index can be read with it before saving.
token.label: Access token
token.hint: Stored in the runtime's secret store, only sent to {{host}}, never shown again.
token.secretOnly: Stored in the runtime's secret store; cicord.yaml did not change.

missing.title: The token is missing on this runtime
missing.hint: cicord.yaml marks this registry as private, but this runtime's secret store has no token for it: its plugins cannot be listed or installed. Set the token again.

confirmRemove.title: Remove the access token of {{name}}?
confirmRemove.text: The registry becomes public in cicord.yaml. If it is private, Cicord can no longer read it. The token is deleted from the secret store when the admin UI created it.

available.title: Update available: {{current}} → {{latest}}
available.text: Review what the new version requests before updating every instance of the plugin.
available.major: A major version: it may change its settings or behavior.
available.modified: This copy was modified in the repository: updating overwrites the local changes.
available.askAdmin: An admin can review and apply it from the Store.

update.title: Update {{name}}
update.lead: {{current}} → {{latest}}. The version is shared by every instance of the plugin: they are all updated in one commit.

notInstalled.title: This plugin is not installed
notInstalled.text: {{plugin}} has no instance: install it from the Store instead.

upToDate.title: {{name}} is up to date
upToDate.text: Version {{version}} is the latest. Refresh the Store to look for a newer release.

update.nothingNew: The new version requests nothing new.
update.capabilitiesRemoved: Capabilities no longer requested (removed from the grants)

repoChanged.title: The plugin moved to another repository
repoChanged.text: The registry now points to another repository than the one locked in cicord.lock. Make sure the publisher announced it before updating.

update.instancesHint: Each instance's grants are set to what the new version requests.

configInvalid.title_one: The config of {{count}} instance is not valid for {{version}}
configInvalid.title_other: The config of {{count}} instances is not valid for {{version}}
configInvalid.hint: The new version changed its settings. Fix the config of these instances first, then update.

restricted.title: You cannot apply this update
restricted.text: The plugin also runs on {{servers}}, where you are not admin. The version is shared by every instance: an admin of every server where it runs must update it.

modified.title: This copy was modified in the repository
modified.text: plugins/{{name}}/ differs from every released version of the plugin. Updating replaces it with the bundled version: keep your changes elsewhere first.
modified.force: Overwrite the local changes in plugins/{{name}}/

update.confirm: I trust {{publisher}}, the publisher of {{name}} from the unofficial source {{source}}, and grant version {{version}}:
update.confirmNothingNew: nothing new (same capabilities, intents and network access)
update.confirmRequired: Confirm that you trust this unofficial source first.
update.forceRequired: Allow overwriting the local changes first.
update.rejected: The configuration is not valid with the new version

changed.title: The plugin changed since you reviewed it
changed.hint: Its latest version now resolves to different code. Review it again: Cicord only installs the code you reviewed.

modifiedError.title: The copy was modified in the repository
modifiedError.hint: Allow overwriting the local changes, or keep them elsewhere first.

intents.title: A privileged intent is off
intents.hint: Turn it on in the Discord developer portal (Bot → Privileged Gateway Intents), save, then update again.

forbidden.title: You are not admin everywhere the plugin runs
forbidden.hint: Updating changes every server where an instance runs: ask an admin of each of them.

done.title: {{name}} is updated to {{version}}
done.committedNoRev: Committed to git; the runtime has not activated it yet.
done.prText: The update applies once the pull request is merged.

noResults.title: No results
noResults.query: Nothing matches “{{query}}” with these filters. Try another word or clear the search.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.description: Activity of {{server}}: hourly aggregates only, never message content or per-member data.

previous.custom: previous period of the same length

custom.title: Custom range
custom.zone: In your time zone ({{zone}}). The range is rounded outward to whole hours; the dashboard shows UTC.

errors.missing: Enter a start and an end, date and time.
errors.order: The end must be after the start.
errors.tooLong: A range covers at most {{count}} days.
errors.future: The start must be in the past.

noStore.title: This runtime does not record analytics
noStore.text: The runtime runs without an analytics store, so there is nothing to show yet. See the analytics guide to set one up.

empty.title: No activity recorded yet
empty.text: Cicord records hourly aggregates as soon as the bot is connected to the server. The first numbers appear within the hour; daily active members after midnight UTC.

disabled.title: Analytics are off for this server
disabled.text: Nothing is collected. To turn analytics on, set this in the server's YAML, then sync:

paused.title: Collection is paused
paused.text: Analytics are off for this server: the numbers below stop at the last recorded hour. To resume, set this in the server's YAML:

missing.title_one: One group of metrics is not collected
missing.title_other: {{count}} groups of metrics are not collected

chart.keys: Use the left and right arrow keys to read the values
chart.gridKeys: Use the arrow keys to read the values

members.title: Members over time
members.description: Human members (bots excluded), or bot members, then joins, leaves and net growth per period.
members.onlineDescription: Discord's approximate count of members online, idle or do not disturb, bots excluded.

active.title: Daily active members
active.description: Distinct members who chatted, reacted, used a command or joined voice.

messages.title: Messages by channel
messages.description: Messages sent by members (bots excluded): top channels and the rest.

heatmap.title: When members chat
heatmap.description: Messages per weekday and hour, in UTC, over the period.

voice.title: Voice time
voice.byChannelDescription: Member-hours spent in each voice channel.
voice.peakDescription: Most members in voice at the same time.

rankings.invitesDescription: Joins per invite link (vanity URL included).
rankings.agesDescription: Age of the Discord account when it joined.

bots.title: Bot commands over time
bots.description: Commands of every bot of the server, by bot. Other bots are counted when they reply publicly: a command answered only privately is not seen.
bots.usersDescription: Distinct members who used a command of any bot, per day.
bots.usersAverage: Distinct members who used a command of any bot: {{value}} a day on average.
bots.commandsDescription: Commands of every bot, with the bot that answers them.
bots.channelsDescription: Channels where members use bot commands.
bots.componentsDescription: Clicks on the buttons and select menus of Cicord's bots.
bots.tenureDescription: How long members had been in the server when they used a command of Cicord's bots.

heatmap.title: When members use bots
heatmap.description: Bot commands per weekday and hour, in UTC, over the period.

empty.title: No bot command used in this period
empty.text: Commands appear here as members use them: Cicord's bots always, other bots when they reply publicly.

tenure.day: Joined less than a day ago
tenure.week: Joined less than a week ago
tenure.month: Joined less than a month ago
tenure.year: Joined less than a year ago
tenure.older: Joined a year ago or more

off.title: Detailed presence is off
off.text: Only Discord's approximate online count is recorded. Statuses, platforms and games need the privileged Presence intent.
off.fix: Set spec.analytics.presence: true in the server's YAML, enable Presence Intent for the bot in the Discord Developer Portal and add ServerPresences to the bot's intents.

presence.shareDescription: Share of the online members sampled over the period.
presence.activitiesDescription: Peak members doing it at the same time over the period.

banner.title: Enforcement is paused
banner.text: Cicord applies nothing to this server: changes made on Discord stay, new revisions and syncs wait.

dialog.title: Pause enforcement?
dialog.text: Use it during an emergency, e.g. a raid: Cicord stops applying the configuration to this server until it is resumed, so the changes you make on Discord (a locked channel) stay. Plans and drift keep being computed. Every pause is in the audit log and the history.

resumeDialog.title: Resume enforcement?
resumeDialog.text: Cicord applies the configuration again: the next revision or sync applies this plan and reverts what changed on Discord during the pause.
resumeDialog.noPlan: The pending plan cannot be computed

pause.badgeHint: Enforcement is paused: nothing is applied to this server until it is resumed.

live.reconnectingHint: Live updates are paused: the runtime is unreachable (restarting or network). The console retries and refreshes every 30 s meanwhile.
live.updatedHint: Reload to use the console of the new version.
